paragraph.text: Now, to analyze the event-free survival times across the 28 days of follow-up, Fig. 3A presents the cumulative incidence curves for the proportion of patients surviving and not receiving attentive care. In contrast to Fig. 2A, these curves are constructed while treating death as a competing risk [11][12][13]. That is, patients who die were removed from the risk set and no longer eligible to experience recovery. The areas below these cumulative incidence curves (Figs. 3B & C) represent the mean event-free survival times up to day 28 [14]. These were 11.9 days for placebo, and 14.2 days for remdesivir. The difference was 2.2 days (95% CI, 0.89 to 3.52 days; P < 0.001) in favor of remdesivir. Thus, on average, patients receiving remdesivir survived event-free for an additional 2.2 days across the 28 days of follow-up. Note that the difference in mean event-free survival is highly statistically significant in favor of remdesivir in contrast to the moderately significant difference obtained using the duration of the need for medical attention. This may reflect the fact that remdesivir numerically prolonged patients' survival [14].

original_verification.explanation: The source Figure 3 caption states: "B and C. Mean time in recovery, as the area under the cumulative incidence curve, across the 28 days of study follow-up." The text similarly states: "the area under the cumulative recovery curve is the average postrecovery time that study patients spent." These statements refer to the same entity as the claim: the areas under the cumulative incidence curves in Figures 3B and 3C for the ACTT-1 recovery analysis over 28 days. The source defines that area as mean time in recovery / average postrecovery time, not mean event-free survival time. Calling it event-free survival changes the outcome being summarized and is therefore substantively incompatible with the source, rather than an ordinary paraphrase.

defender.analysis: The cited paper directly describes the same figure panels: "B and C. Mean time in recovery, as the area under the cumulative incidence curve, across the 28 days of study follow-up." The text likewise states that "the area under the cumulative recovery curve is the average postrecovery time that study patients spent" and reports that "patients receiving remdesivir spent 14.1 postrecovery days, on average, whereas patients receiving placebo spent only 11.9 days." This supports the geometric area and the 28-day window, but it rules out the claim's core characterization as "mean event-free survival times." In the same ACTT-1 recovery-curve analysis, the area under the cumulative incidence of recovery is post-recovery time, not event-free survival time; event-free survival would correspond to the complement/area under the not-recovered curve. Thus the source's explicit interpretation is substantively incompatible with 'event-free survival.'
key_points: Figures 3B and 3C are indeed the cumulative incidence-curve panels, and their areas are summarized over 28 days.
The source defines the area as 'mean time in recovery' or 'average postrecovery time,' not as event-free survival time.
The reported mean values (11.9 and 14.1 days; the manuscript rounds 14.1 to 14.2) refer to postrecovery days, which changes the interpretation.

prosecutor.analysis: The claim mislabels the quantity represented by the areas under the cumulative incidence curves. The cited source explicitly states that "the area under the cumulative recovery curve is the average postrecovery time that study patients spent" and the Figure 3 caption calls panels B and C "Mean time in recovery, as the area under the cumulative incidence curve, across the 28 days of study follow-up." This is not the mean event-free survival time; it is restricted mean time in recovery / average postrecovery time. The same entity is at issue: Figures 3B and 3C for the ACTT-1 recovery cumulative incidence curves over 28 days. Calling this "event-free survival" changes the outcome being summarized and would mislead readers about the direction and meaning of the area. The numerical discrepancy between 14.1 and 14.2 days is minor and not the core problem.
key_points: Figures 3B and 3C are described by the source as showing mean time in recovery / average postrecovery time, not mean event-free survival time.

The area under a cumulative recovery incidence curve measures time spent recovered up to day 28; a restricted mean event-free survival quantity would come from a survival curve, not a recovery cumulative incidence curve.
This is a material scientific mislabeling rather than a faithful paraphrase or ordinary simplification.
The 14.1 vs 14.2 day difference is minor/rounding and not the basis for the objection.
